title: Solar eclipse 2026 across Europe: in pictures
text:
A total solar eclipse swept across parts of Europe and the North Atlantic on 12 August, with the path of totality moving through Greenland, Iceland, Spain and a small section of north-eastern Portugal, while surrounding areas across Europe experienced a partial solar eclipse, according to the European Space Agency
Teruel, Spain
The moon completely covers the sun during a total solar eclipse as seen from the Javalambre Astrophysical Observatory in Arcos de las Salinas. Photograph: Christian Hartmann/Reuters
The sun’s corona glows as the moon completely blocks the sun during the totality phase of the total solar eclipsePhotograph: Ander Gillenea/AFP/Getty Images
Local Faro residents watch the solar eclipse at the Parque Ribeirinho, at a viewing event organised by the Algarve Science CentrePhotograph: David Levene/The Guardian
People excitedly watch the partial solar eclipse at Abbadia, le Château Observatoire. France will not see another total eclipse for 55 yearsPhotograph: Philippe Lopez/AFP/Getty Images
Hundreds of people secure viewing spots on and around the historic Krakus Mound (Kopiec Krakusa) ahead of the solar eclipsePhotograph: Artur Widak/NurPhoto/Shutterstock
Passengers on board the Ambassador cruise ship Ambition are among the first to see the solar eclipse off the coast of GreenlandPhotograph: Owen Humphreys/PA
The sun during a partial solar eclipse, partly obscured by clouds, with the International Space Station silhouetted against it as the craft transits at roughly five miles a secondPhotograph: Nasa Handout/EPA
The moon completely covers the sun during a total solar eclipse as seen from the Javalambre Astrophysical Observatory in Arcos de las Salinas.Photograph: Christian Hartmann/Reuters
Beachgoers watch a solar eclipse as the moon partially covers the sun and briefly dims the afternoon light along the coastPhotograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters
